results.claim: THEOREM 3.6: there is an absolute δ>0 with Σ_{n≤x} λ(n)λ(n+1) ≪ (1−δ)x, giving no decay, with the shift h=1; quoted from the abstract (third consequence) of Matomäki–Radziwiłł arXiv:1501.04585.
results.paper_quote: Abstract: "Third, we show that the mean-value of λ(n)λ(n+1), with λ(n) Liouville's function, is non-trivially bounded in absolute value by 1 − δ for some δ > 0. This settles an old folklore conjecture and constitutes progress towards Chowla's conjecture." Numbered form, Corollary 2: "For every integer h ≥ 1, there exists δ(h) > 0 such that (1/X)|Σ_{n≤X} λ(n)λ(n+h)| ≤ 1 − δ(h) for all large enough X > 1."
results.doc_quote: "There is an absolute δ > 0 with Σ_{n≤x} λ(n) λ(n+1) ≪ (1 − δ) x." / abstract, third consequence: "we show that the mean-value of λ(n)λ(n+1) … is non-trivially bounded in absolute value by 1 − δ for some δ > 0. This settles an old folklore conjecture and constitutes progress towards Chowla's conjecture."
results.notes: Read arXiv HTML v4 §1 plus the abs page, and compared the v1 abs page. The quoted abstract sentence is verbatim (the ellipsis hides only ", with λ(n) Liouville's function,"). In the paper the numbered form is Corollary 2, where δ = δ(h) may depend on h; the doc fixes h = 1, so an absolute δ(1) is legitimate. Minor notational looseness: it writes "≪ (1−δ)x" and drops the absolute-value bars and "for all large enough X", but its gloss ("bounds the mean value ... in absolute value") restores both. Abstract text identical in v1 and v4; no numbered result cited, so no numbering conflict. Journal ref Ann. of Math. 183(3) (2016) 1015–1056 confirmed.

results.claim: Row T5, two clauses: (a) Σ_{n≤x} λ(n)λ(n+1) ≪ (1−δ)x for some δ>0; (b) μ cancels in almost all short intervals [x, x+ψ(x)] with ψ(x) → ∞ arbitrarily slowly, i.e. the Möbius sum over the interval is o of its length for almost every x.
results.paper_quote: Abstract: "First, for the Möbius function we show that there are cancellations in the sum of μ(n) in almost all intervals of the form [x, x + ψ(x)] with ψ(x) → ∞ arbitrarily slowly." Corollary 2: "For every integer h ≥ 1, there exists δ(h) > 0 such that (1/X)|Σ_{n≤X} λ(n)λ(n+h)| ≤ 1 − δ(h) for all large enough X > 1."
results.doc_quote: "Σ_{n≤x}λ(n)λ(n+1) ≪ (1−δ)x for some δ > 0; μ cancels in almost all short intervals [x, x+ψ(x)], ψ → ∞" and the gloss "the Möbius sum over the interval is o of its length for almost every x, with ψ(x) → ∞ arbitrarily slowly."
results.notes: Read arXiv HTML v4 (abstract, Theorem 1, Corollary 2) plus the abs page. Clause (a) is the abstract's third consequence / Corollary 2 (δ = δ(h) in general; h = 1 gives an absolute constant, exactly the shift the row uses). Clause (b) is the abstract's first consequence verbatim; the quantitative engine is Theorem 1 with f = μ, whose exceptional set C·X((log h)^{1/3}/(δ²h^{δ/25}) + 1/(δ²(log X)^{1/50})) is o(X) as h = ψ(x) → ∞, so "almost every x" and "arbitrarily slowly" are faithful. Annals ref confirmed (CaltechAUTHORS record, DOI 10.4007/annals.2016.183.3.6); the doc's hedge that it is unconfirmed is harmless.

results.claim: THEOREM 3.8: Tao's arXiv:1509.05422 result holds for k = 2 and every fixed affine pair with a_1b_2 − a_2b_1 ≠ 0, in particular (1/log x) Σ_{n≤x} λ(n)λ(n+2)/n = o(1); the parity barrier is broken only in the logarithmically averaged sense; the entropy decrement method rests on MR arXiv:1501.04585 on short intervals.
results.paper_quote: Tao, Theorem 1.2 (Logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture): "Let a_1,a_2 be natural numbers, and let b_1,b_2 be integers such that a_1b_2 − a_2b_1 ≠ 0. Let 1 ≤ ω(x) ≤ x be a quantity depending on x that goes to infinity as x → ∞. Then Σ_{x/ω(x)<n≤x} λ(a_1n+b_1)λ(a_2n+b_2)/n = o(log ω(x)) as n → ∞." Abstract: "... thus breaking the 'parity barrier' for this problem."
results.doc_quote: "Definition 3.7 holds for k = 2 and every fixed affine pair with a_1 b_2 − a_2 b_1 ≠ 0. In particular (1/log x) Σ_{n≤x} λ(n) λ(n+2)/n = o(1)." ... "The method is the entropy decrement argument, resting on Matomäki–Radziwiłł, arXiv:1501.04585 on short intervals."
results.notes: This document's claim rests on 1509.05422, which I also read (HTML v4 §1, abs v1 and v4). Theorem 1.2 matches Definition 3.7 with k = 2 verbatim in scope (a_i natural, b_i integers, a_1b_2−a_2b_1 ≠ 0, 1 ≤ ω(x) ≤ x, ω → ∞); ω(x) = x gives the doc's λ(n)λ(n+2)/n instance, the dropped n = 1 term being O(1/log x). The doc cites v1 17 Sep 2015 / v4 29 Jul 2016 and the parity-barrier sentence is in both; numbering checked in v4 only. Dependency note: Tao's intro routes the short-sum estimate through the three-author paper [23], based in turn on [21] = 1501.04585, while the abstract names the three-author result directly, so resting on MR is fair but indirect.
